_comment: DEEP mutation run — `npm run test:mutation:deep`. Everything `stryker.config.json` runs,
plus the INTEGRATION suites. Not a replacement for that file: a second, slower measurement
answering a different question.
The default run executes unit and cross-cutting tests only. That is the right scope for a
gate — it is fast enough to run per commit — but it means every file whose tests live in
`tests/integration/` is measured with a ruler configured not to touch it, and scores 0% for
a reason that has nothing to do with how well it is tested. As of 2026-08-27 that was 3186
of `src/modules/`'s 5489 mutants: 58% of the module scope, reported as NoCoverage.
MEASURED, on `src/modules/products/repository.ts` (196 mutants), 2026-08-27:
| scope                   | score  | NoCoverage | wall clock |
| unit only (the default) |  0.00% | 161        | —          |
| + integration (here)    | 82.14% |   3        | 22m 13s    |
The tests were always there and they are good. What the 0% measured was the scope.
Wall clock. 196 mutants took 22 minutes here against roughly one second each under the unit
scope, because an integration mutant runs a suite that talks to a real in-memory Mongo and,
for a repository, 45 of those 196 mutants made a query HANG — each one paying `timeoutMS`
in full before being recorded as killed. Extrapolated over `src/modules/`, this is a
multi-hour run: a nightly, not a gate.
`tests/contract/` and `tests/fuzz/` stay out even here. A contract test boots the whole app
through supertest, so `enableFindRelatedTests` relates it to very nearly every file in the
project — which would make each mutant pay a full application boot, and would relate a
one-line change in one module to the entire contract suite. Fuzz suites are non-deterministic
by construction; a mutant killed by a random input on one run and not the next produces a
score that moves on its own.
This run writes to `reports/mutation-deep/` and keeps its own incremental file. It does NOT
feed `mutation-baseline.json`: the ratchet compares like with like, and a baseline recorded
from a wider scope would fail every subsequent default run as a mass regression. Compare a
deep run against the PREVIOUS deep run, by eye or by report.
